thread:
maddie: quick idea — I'm building a tiny 'jitter playground' sample app to reproduce 429 bursts + token-rotation cases. want to check SDK behavior on retries and unsafe replays. posting the minimal harness below, feedback? :thinking:

sanjay: love this. do we have a hypothesis? are duplicates showing up only after auth refresh or also on plain 429 retries?

maddie: mostly after refresh combined with short backoff windows. some requests re-run without idempotency keys. hypothesis: SDKs resume with naive replay when the stream reconnects.

leo: fwiw Node SDK today will attempt a resume and may replay last in-flight request if the client hasn't attached an idempotency key. python sdk doesn't expose a safe_replay_window config yet. :grimacing:

alex: here's a minimal curl + JS harness I used locally (gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/jitter-play). snippet:

```
// pseudo
const opts = { retries: { max: 6, jitter: { min: 50, max: 600 } }, idempotency: true }
await sdk.call("/v1/generate", { prompt }, opts)
```

ryan: small suggestion — add a unique Idempotency-Key header for all stateful endpoints. That makes replays safe even if SDK reissues.

maddie: thanks. question: should SDKs default to sending an Idempotency-Key for any POST-like call? might be surprising for users but increases safety.

sanjay: tradeoffs: collisions and semantics for pure-analytics events. maybe opt-in by default, but enable auto-key for calls that change server state (e.g., create fine-tune, accepted-chat-message).

leo: another angle — expose a "safe_replay_window_ms" config so integrators can tune how long the SDK will try to resume vs. restart. then SDKs can bias towards exponential backoff + full jitter inside that window.

maddie: sketching an experiment: 1) auto-idempotency + short safe_replay_window (500ms) 2) auto-idempotency + longer window (2s) 3) no auto-key, rely on explicit keys. run each under spike of 429s and token rotation and measure duplicates.

dev-bot: deploybot: canary test harness deployed to staging (run id: jitter-2026-03-23-01) :white_check_mark:

alex: quick gotcha: when using streaming responses, resumable streams may replay partial tokens. make sure the harness logs sequence numbers + idempotency keys so we can detect partial duplicates.

maddie: good point. I'll add per-message sequence ids to the harness and a small dedupe checker.

ryan: also capture timing distribution — backoff windows, jitter samples, and when token-refresh happened. those correlate strongly with duplicates in our past postmortems.

sanjay: for SDK parity: let's add the python flag and a Go binding in the same PR so we can test cross-SDK behavior. keep the defaults conservative (no auto-key) but provide a one-line opt-in: { auto_idempotency: true }.

maddie: plan: push harness + results.csv to the repo under /tools/jitter-play, open draft PR w/ python + node patches. tagging folks for review. thanks all :rocket:
thread_summary: experiment plan for jitter/backoff/idempotency harness to measure duplicates during 429 spikes + token rotations, discussion about auto-idempotency, safe replay windows, SDK parity, and streaming replay edgecases
